title: Why the list is slow on purpose
headline: Why the list says −56% when the price says $35.
dek: The board's 7-day change compares the median of three readings at each end of the week, not one reading against one. On Nov 7, Pikachu ex 107's last three readings were $74.19 (Nov 4), $68.40 (Nov 5) and $35.30 (Nov 6). Their median, $68.40, against $156.08 a week earlier is −56.2%, while the latest reading was already $35.30. We chose that rule on Oct 13 so one day's spike can't pass for a weekly move. This week's halving shows its cost: the list is slow on purpose.
why_now: Tuesday's and Thursday's Files ran into the same thing: a list that says down after a price has turned. The nightly File that now writes the hero shows it on every row, so this is the Saturday to say how the number is built and what that choice costs.
risk: A smoothed change isn't wrong, it is late: after a real turn it keeps reading the old direction for about a week. A raw one-reading change is current but gets fooled by one thin sale, like the one-sale jump that first sent us to medians (Snorlax Lv.X, +41.7%, Oct 2026). We picked slow over fooled; that is a judgment. The table's start price (a median) sits beside the latest reading (a single reading), so a row can look like it doesn't add up. Showing the end median beside it is on our list, not built. No sale was checked behind this move. This is not a read on whether the price is high or low.
what_to_watch: Whether we show the end-of-week median beside the latest price so a row adds up (not built yet). Whether Pikachu ex 107 leaves the 7-day list around Nov 13 and Nov 14, as the rule says it should once the week it compares against stops containing pre-Nov 6 readings. And the Files: Thursday's stands through Saturday, this one through Tuesday, and the nightly File returns Wednesday.
source: TCGplayer market prices via tcgcsv.com, the board's lists of Nov 5 to Nov 7, 2026 (readings Nov 4 to Nov 6) and Mission Control's board settings (3-day medians, set Oct 13, 2026)

foot: Market price: TCGplayer's average of recent completed sales of the same card, condition and printing (help.tcgplayer.com). The worked example: Pikachu ex 107's readings on the board's lists, $156.08 as the median of the three days ending Oct 30, $74.19, $68.40 and $35.30 on Nov 4, Nov 5 and Nov 6; $68.40 / $156.08 − 1 = −56.2%. The rule: Mission Control's WEEK_SMOOTH_DAYS = 3 (config/board.py), set Oct 13, 2026, so a price that spikes for a day can't make a weekly move and a day-old reading at the far end can't fake one. The list: up to 10 Pokémon cards worth $20 or more that moved 5% or more in a week; with no checked sales, a move shows only if it's 60% or less, the lowest listing moved the same way by at least a quarter as much, the price changed in the last 2 days, and the card trades. Unconfirmed: no sale checked by Mission Control's Sale Integrity Layer in that window. Not advice.
